text: Day counter inconsistent: Chronicle says 'Day 5, morning', Season panel says 'Autumn - day 1/2, year 1', state.json day=4. Three different day numbers for the same moment.
Floating settlement label ('0 here, 1/8 residents') renders huge and is cut off by the top edge of the screen right after founding, overlapping the chronicle panel.

In-settlement HUD: objective progress bar text is clipped on the left ('mbers 9/10 * Buildings 2/2'), Settlement Info 'Next (K): House, 20 wood, 1...' is cut off on the right, and Settlement Info says 'Tier: Town (5 buildings)' while the era badge says 'Camp (1/4)'.

Settlement action buttons reflow whenever the nearest pawn changes (Gift/Order/Talk buttons appear and move), so Build Farm/Build House shift position between the first click and the confirm click. My first 'Confirm Build Farm' click just re-armed the confirm instead of building (status 'Click again to confirm: Build Farm. (x2)').

World event 'Wanderers at the gate' offers 'Welcome them all (4 food) - fed from your stores', but no HUD panel shows the settlement's food stores, so the player cannot judge whether 4 food is affordable going into winter (tick 141552).
Trying to feed a resident in winter: G / 'Gift <pawn>' always gives 10 coins ('Coins? That's generous of you.'), there is no option to give apples or other food to a hungry NPC (#353).

First winter, day 1: three NPCs die of hunger (Fiona Robinson tick 195253, Nancy Williams 199797, Samantha Brown 200565). The top status toast just says 'Samantha Brown has died.' with no nation or cause; only the truncated chronicle line says she 'starved within the walls' of Castleford. No hunger warning preceded any death, and nothing on screen shows food or hunger for my own 15 residents, so I cannot tell whether my town is next or how to feed them.

Player energy never drains while standing inside the settlement (92.4 flat for 25,000+ ticks in winter), while outdoors winter roughly doubles drain (1 apple auto-eaten per ~2,000 ticks vs ~3,000 in autumn). Sheltering in town makes the player's winter trivial; the auto-eat also means the player never makes a food decision.
